lines.text: Welcome to the 3HUE lobby. I'm {guide}, the platform 3HUE built. 3HUE's managed programs run on me, and today I'm your guide.
lines.source: The Message Stack §09, boilerplate

lines.text: There are three doors here. Each one is a different trigger, a different buyer and a different first sentence. Behind all three is the same thing: a program someone runs, and can prove.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments

lines.text: Tell me who I'm walking with, and I'll start you at the right door.
lines.source: Tour script, linking line

lines.text: {door:win-trust.title}. This room is for {door:win-trust.icp} whose next contract depends on evidence they can't produce yet.
lines.source: The Forcing Function, cover; §02, the three segments

lines.text: Before I show you anything, tell me what's pressing. The answer changes what matters in here.
lines.source: Tour script, linking line

options.label: Nobody's asking yet
options.sub: No deal, renewal or insurer on the clock

lines.text: Then you need two things fast: a readiness letter with a date on it, and someone negotiating scope, so you build only what the contract requires.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §04, trigger events; §02, the three segments

lines.text: Then the fix isn't a faster scramble. It's evidence that regenerates instead of being reassembled every time someone with leverage asks.
lines.source: The Message Stack §03, three pillars; The Forcing Function, cover

lines.text: Then four questions matter: what can it access, what can it change, who approved it, and what proves it stayed inside.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §04, trigger events

lines.text: The AI Risk & Readiness Snapshot is framed around exactly those questions. On the service list, the follow-on is {offer:ai-governance-advisory}.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §04, trigger events; The Message Stack §05, claims library; 3HUE service catalog

lines.text: Then you may be early, and 3HUE would rather tell you that than sell you something. Here the trigger is usually a deal, a renewal or an insurer with a date.
lines.source: The Ship List §06, discovery script; The Forcing Function §02, the three segments; §05, who to decline

lines.text: The constraint isn't knowledge. It's capacity. The frameworks are public; what's missing is someone to run them.
lines.source: The Message Stack §01, core narrative

lines.text: 3HUE's view: you get the report because your buyer needs it, and a program because you need it.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

lines.text: Tell me what's pressing. Nobody buys maturity on principle. They buy it when a customer, an insurer, an investor or a regulator makes them.

lines.text: Then the fix is one control set across every company, and reporting the investment committee can read without a translator.

lines.text: That gap isn't a philosophy difference. It's a staffing one.

lines.text: {door:stay-ready.title}. This room is for banks, credit unions, lenders and operators with governance on paper and an examiner in the building.
lines.source: The Forcing Function, cover

lines.text: Here the conversation can be in the examiner's language from the first sentence. So, what's pressing?
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments; The Message Stack §04, the message by segment

options.label: Nobody's asking yet
options.sub: No exam, finding or board mandate on the clock

lines.text: Then the job is findings that close and stay closed, with evidence that survives the next exam, not just this one.
lines.source: The Message Stack §04, the message by segment; The Forcing Function §04, trigger events

lines.text: Then the question is whether you can demonstrate, on the worst day, that what you said was true was actually true.
lines.source: The Ship List §04, LinkedIn post series

lines.text: That usually means a response plan, playbooks and a tabletop exercise, so the team has rehearsed before it has to respond for real.
lines.source: 3HUE service catalog, as listed in this room's services

lines.text: Then map it to the frameworks your examiner already uses.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments

lines.text: For AI, ask four questions of every use: what can it access, what can it change, who approved it, and what proves it stayed inside.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §04, trigger events

lines.text: Then you may be early, and 3HUE would rather tell you that than sell you something. Here the trigger is usually an exam finding, a remediation clock or a board mandate.
lines.source: The Ship List §06, discovery script; The Forcing Function §02, the three segments; §05, who to decline

lines.text: Deployed is not operating. The gap between the two is where both audits and incidents happen.
lines.source: The Message Stack §01, core narrative; §08, words we use

lines.text: In this room the buyer is a peer, not a novice, so the practitioner's own record matters more than any case study.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments

lines.text: In this room the CEO or COO signs. The CTO or VP Engineering champions it, and increasingly so does the Head of Sales whose deal is blocked.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments

lines.text: The lead investor, outside counsel and the insurance broker influence it. There's usually no CISO in the room. That's the gap 3HUE fills.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments; The Message Stack §06, objection handling

lines.text: In a fund, the operating partner or fund CFO signs. Portfolio-company CTOs and the value-creation team champion it.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments

lines.text: The deal team, the insurance broker and the lender influence it. They think in portfolios and exits, not in controls.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments

lines.text: Here the CIO, CISO or Chief Risk Officer signs, with the audit committee behind them. Internal audit, the examiner's letter and the board influence it.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments

lines.text: Each of them needs to hear something different, and the case that convinces the champion rarely convinces the person who signs.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §03, the buying committee

lines.text: The CEO or COO hears about security when a deal, a renewal or a policy is at risk. Never before.

lines.text: They ask what it costs, how long it takes, and whether it closes the deal.

lines.text: What they need to hear: a fixed-scope start with a date, the deal it unblocks, and the person who scopes the work on the call, not a junior team.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §03, the buying committee; The Message Stack §05, claims library

lines.text: The operating partner or fund CFO answers to an investment committee. They want oversight across entities without hiring a CISO for each one.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §03, the buying committee; §02, the three segments

lines.text: They ask what the exposure is across the portfolio, and whether the policy will pay out.

lines.text: What they need to hear: one control set across every company, evidence that survives diligence, and reporting a board can read without a translator.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §03, the buying committee

lines.text: The CIO, CISO or Chief Risk Officer answers to a board and an examiner. What they fear is a finding that won't close, or a voided claim after an incident.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §03, the buying committee; §02, the three segments

lines.text: What they need to hear: findings that close and stay closed, named frameworks in the examiner's language, and reporting a board can read without a translator.
lines.source: The Message Stack §04, the message by segment; The Forcing Function §03, the buying committee

lines.text: They ask you to tell them what they don't have to do. And they ask who is actually going to run this.

lines.text: What they need to hear: the scope cut to what the standard requires, and 3HUE's line on the rest. We don't hand you a plan. We run the program.

lines.text: The person holding the deadline is often the Head of Sales. They know nothing about controls, but they're holding the procurement email that killed the deal.

lines.text: What they say is: we're losing to a worse product because they seemed more legit.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §03, the buying committee

lines.text: What they need to hear: a readiness letter with a date for procurement, and someone who owns the questionnaire. The competitor that won wasn't better. They were provable.

intro.text: Ask me about 3HUE. I answer only from 3HUE's approved material, and every answer shows where it comes from.

questions.q: What is 3HUE?

lines.text: 3HUE builds and operates security, compliance and AI governance programs for organizations that have to prove their controls work — and have no one inside to run them.
lines.source: The Message Stack §09, boilerplate

questions.q: How is 3HUE different from a consultant?

lines.text: Two things. 3HUE runs the program instead of handing you a plan, and the same advisor who scopes the work delivers it.
lines.source: The Message Stack §03, three pillars; §05, claims library

lines.text: The managed programs run on me, so the evidence stays current between audits.
lines.source: The Message Stack §01, core narrative; §09, boilerplate

questions.q: Where do we start?

lines.text: You finish with a straight answer on whether you'll pass, a scoped plan with a date, and the list of things you don't have to do.
lines.source: The Ship List §03, landing page copy

questions.q: What happens after the Snapshot?

lines.text: Then {ref:arc.1} and {ref:arc.2}. If you want 3HUE to run the program, it does.
lines.source: The lobby's Snapshot, Build, Operate; The Ship List §03, landing page copy

lines.text: If you'd rather take the plan and run it yourself, that works too, and you'll have something an internal hire can inherit rather than start over.
lines.source: The Ship List §03, landing page copy

questions.q: How does pricing work?

lines.text: Pricing is scoped, so there's no list price here. The Snapshot ends with a scoped plan: how long, what it costs, and who does the work.
lines.source: The Ship List §03, landing page copy; §06, discovery script

lines.text: Price it against the deal, exam or exit that's waiting on it, not against a tool subscription. For a figure, talk to the team.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling; The Forcing Function §01, the fit model

questions.q: We already pay for a compliance platform. Why would we need you?

lines.text: Keep it. A platform tells you what's wrong. The question is who fixes it, who answers the questionnaire, and who negotiates scope with the auditor.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

lines.text: That's the job 3HUE does, on top of the tool you already bought.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

questions.q: Isn't this just compliance theater?

lines.text: Mostly, yes. A certificate says controls existed during a window.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

lines.text: That's why 3HUE sells the operating layer, not the certificate: you get the report because your buyer needs it, and a program because you need it.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

questions.q: Can you guarantee we pass?

lines.text: No, and be careful with anyone who says otherwise.
lines.source: The Ship List §03, landing page copy

lines.text: What 3HUE can do is tell you before you start whether you'll pass, scope the work to what the standard actually requires, and manage the auditor so there are no surprises.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

questions.q: Why not just hire a CISO?

lines.text: Eventually you should. At your size, a full-time hire would be under-used for the first year.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

lines.text: 3HUE runs the program now and builds it so that hire inherits something rather than starting over.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

questions.q: Our MSP already handles security. Where do you fit?

lines.text: Ask them three questions: which framework are we assessed against, who signs off on risk acceptance, and what happens when an auditor challenges a control?
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

lines.text: If the answers are good, you're in fine shape. If they're vague, that's the gap 3HUE fills, alongside your MSP, not instead of it.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling; §07, battlecards

questions.q: How is this different from a big-firm readiness engagement?

lines.text: Here, the person in the room is the person doing the work, and the scope stays where it was set.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

lines.text: And when the report is delivered, 3HUE is still running the program. Continuity is usually the difference that matters.
lines.source: The Message Stack §06, objection handling

questions.q: Which frameworks do you work with?

lines.text: It depends on who is asking you to prove it. For a bank, a credit union or a lender, 3HUE works in the frameworks the examiner already uses.
lines.source: The Forcing Function §02, the three segments; The Message Stack §04, the message by segment

lines.text: For a software company selling into enterprise, the usual ask is SOC 2 or ISO 27001. The service list also includes {offer:iso-27701-pims-readiness-implementation}.
